combo_label: Breakfast × Puppets & Punch and Judy × Roald Dahl

entries.clue: Big flightless Australian bird, and the name of a famously unruly arm puppet
Wreck a plane on landing, as Dahl did in the desert in 1940
Dark hardy grain behind a dense Nordic bread and an American whiskey
Jim Henson's word for his foam-and-fabric puppets, now British slang for a fool
Sweetshop keeper with filthy black fingernails, loathed by Dahl's gang
Beauregarde girl who swells into a blueberry inside the sweet-maker's works
Adjective the title bestows on Mr Fox, raider of a hidden cider cellar
Hinged pincers that lift hot food onto a plate without scorched fingers
Stretched white sheet a shadow puppet is pressed against, lit from behind
Cured pork strips, smoked or unsmoked, spitting as they crisp
Stayed under the duvet far too long and so missed the usual train
Live dog in a frilled collar once part of the Punch show, and a jug shaped as a man
